title: Bedside tests to triage patients for prehabilitation before major abdominal surgery: accuracy against CPET
subtitle: Diagnostic accuracy study with CPET anaerobic threshold as the reference standard
statement: Prehabilitation places (40 a quarter) are allocated by exercise testing, but the single machine's four-week wait means about half of the 110 patients a quarter are never tested in time. It is not known whether the 30-second sit-to-stand test or four-metre gait speed, done at pre-assessment, can identify patients with an anaerobic threshold below 11 mL/kg/min accurately enough to triage places.
whoAffected: Patients awaiting colorectal, upper gastrointestinal, liver and pancreatic resections, especially older and frail patients; physiotherapists and exercise physiologists; the prehabilitation team allocating 40 places.
whatHurts: Unfit patients who miss prehabilitation because they wait for a test face more complications, and places may go to patients who need them less.
currentPractice: Exercise testing decides priority; untested patients are allocated places by clinical impression when surgery is close.
whyNow: A four-week wait, bedside tests already used by physiotherapists, and an ethics application under review.
patientCenteredGoal: The patients who would gain most from prehabilitation are identified in time to complete it before surgery.
summary: Problem framed as a diagnostic accuracy question for triage to prehabilitation.
